result.summary:
Full TEST-RUNNER pass for REQ-171 on branch feature/WF02-REQ171-20260828 at commit e95185b. docker compose (postgres on port 5463 per untracked .env LETFLOW_DB_PORT, keycloak) already running and healthy. All commands run with PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" and WASMEX_BUILD=true.

1) mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force: 'Compiling 136 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', exit 0. Clean, no warnings.

2) mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/: 'Finished in 10.8 seconds (0.00s async, 10.8s sync)' / 'Result: 119 passed' -- matches TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's expected count of 119 exactly. Two pre-existing Dialyzer-style type-check warnings noted from module_registry_test.exs (ModuleRegistry.register(nil) / register(42) given non-binary args to test the documented FunctionClauseError guard) -- these are compiler type-warnings on intentionally-invalid test inputs, not test failures, and did not affect the warnings-as-errors compile step above (compile step ran clean because these warnings are emitted only during mix test's own compile-in-context, not the app compile). Three GenServer.call timeout stack traces logged at 500ms/300ms/7000ms against a function literally named "hang" -- these are REQ-170's intentional hang-path tests exercising ISS-0352's known wasmex native-thread-pool exhaustion hazard; each resolved within its own configured timeout and the run still finished at 119/119 passed, so this is the known, mitigated background hazard recurring as expected, not a new failure.

3) scripts/test_parallel.sh (full suite, N=8 partitions via nproc): all 8 partitions exit 0, 0 failures each. Combined: 'combined: 2402 tests, 5 properties, 0 failures (2407/2407 passed)'. No occurrences of ISS-0287 (pool exhaustion) or ISS-0351 (registry timeout-path CPU-spin) signatures in any partition log.

4) mix letflow.lint_handoffs: 'letflow.lint_handoffs: OK -- 0 new violations across 1284 handoff files (25 pre-existing grandfathered, traced to ISS-0190).' This handoff file (step-04-test-runner.json) is not among the flagged files.

No failures anywhere in the suite -- no test/reports/ file written per the project's convention that a clean pass needs no report file. No structural attribution needed since nothing failed.
